QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_20

question.text: Yamuna AIF drew INR 50 crore at t=0. Over 5 years, its terminal distribution (ignoring fees) is INR 70 crore. Approximate Gross IRR?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Solve 50 = 70/(1+IRR)^5, giving (1+IRR)^5 = 1.40. Taking the 5th root: 1+IRR ≈ 1.0696, so IRR ≈ 6.96%. This matches the worst-case in the PDF Example 7.1. **The Trap:** 8% rounds up. 4% is too low. 10% is the hurdle rate, not the IRR. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests identical shortcut. XXI-B uses CAGR on NAV, not XIRR — different formula but similar intuition. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Use '(FV/PV)^(1/n) - 1' as a quick single-flow IRR check in IC meetings. If the full XIRR model disagrees materially, you have a cash-flow data error.
